_meta.description: DISPOSABLE proof-of-concept flow. Confirms two things before the production Appraisal Review Extractor flow/topic are rebuilt around Execute Agent: (1) whether a file attached via Execute Agent's advanced 'attachments' parameter can actually be read inside a Copilot Studio topic, and (2) the real shape of Execute Agent and wait's response. QUESTION 2 IS NOW ANSWERED against a real tenant: the connector call succeeds, 'lastResponse' is the correct field name, and it arrives as an already-parsed Object requiring no json() step. Question 1's answer is whatever 'attachmentReceived=' value the raw-response message shows. Delete this flow, agent/poc-attachment-echo-topic.yaml, and the throwaway PoC agent once both questions are answered.
connectors: Microsoft Copilot Studio (shared_CopilotStudio or your tenant's equivalent connector id) — Execute Agent and wait, against a THROWAWAY PoC agent, not the production one
Microsoft Teams (shared_teams) — Post message in a channel, purely so the result is easy to eyeball without opening run history
_meta.buildNote: Build the 'Execute Agent and wait' action from the live connector picker in Power Automate, not by pasting this file's 'actions.Execute_Agent_And_Wait' block — the exact operation path/schema for this action is not something this repo has verified against a real tenant yet; that is the entire point of this PoC. See POC.md for the build steps and what each possible outcome means.

trigger.description: 'Manually trigger a flow' with a File-type input, same mechanism the production design uses — reusing it here also incidentally re-confirms the Teams file-upload-to-flow path still works.

Build_Data_Uri.description: CONFIRMED against a real tenant: a File-type input on a manual trigger resolves to an OBJECT with 'contentBytes' and 'name' properties — NOT a plain base64 string. Referencing triggerBody()?['testFile'] directly stringifies the whole object into the URI (producing 'data:application/pdf;base64,{"contentBytes":"JVBERi0x...') and fails with error code InvalidUriContent. Drill into ?['contentBytes'] as below. Also note: no whitespace anywhere in the data URI prefix — 'data: application/pdf' with a space is invalid.

Execute_Agent_And_Wait.description: PLACEHOLDER — build this action from the connector picker: search 'Copilot Studio' > 'Execute Agent and wait'. Point it at the throwaway PoC agent (not production). Message/body: the literal text 'poc echo attachment' (must match the PoC topic's trigger phrase exactly). Under Advanced parameters, find the attachments field and supply one attachment: name = testFileFileName, contentType = application/pdf, contentUrl/content = the output of Build_Data_Uri. The 'path' below is not a real, verified operation id — do not paste this action, build it live.

Compose_Raw_Response.description: The whole, unmodified response body from Execute Agent and wait — inspect this first. It tells you the real field names regardless of whether the 'lastResponse' assumption below is right.

Extract_LastResponse.description: CONFIRMED against a real tenant: 'lastResponse' IS the correct field name on Execute Agent and wait's response, and it arrives as an already-parsed Object — NOT a JSON string. An earlier version of this action wrapped it in json(), which failed with "the template language function 'json' expects its parameter to be a string or an XML. The provided value is of type 'Object'". No parsing step is needed; reference the field directly. Carry this finding into the production flow — it removes a step the earlier designs assumed was necessary.

Post_Raw_Result_To_Teams.description: Always posts the raw response — this alone is enough to answer question 2 (the real field names/shape), regardless of whether the lastResponse parse attempt below succeeds.

Post_LastResponse_To_Teams.description: Separate, independent post showing just the lastResponse field on its own — the topic's actual reply text, isolated from the rest of the response envelope.

notificationChannelId.description: Any channel you can post test results to — does not need to be the real credit risk channel.
